content_selection.rationale: The main stories are well chosen. Anthropic's eval and internet cutoff, OpenAI's grader misalignment report, the White House disclosure push, the OpenAI revenue correction, Nvidia–Reflection, and the decision-model cluster are all strong, timely picks with a clear unifying theme. However, my searches showed that several excluded stories were widely covered and fit the brief's agent-safety theme better than some of the 'Briefly' fillers. Examples: the fired OpenAI safety researchers' open letter, SemiAnalysis's finding that only 3.6% of Chinese model releases published safety results, and the Senate investigation into data-center costs. Meanwhile, Cloudflare acquiring Deno is not really AI news, and the Perplexity embedding release is minor. Most noticeably, the brief leaves out OpenAI's own safety-culture dispute while giving a full section to industry-wide agent misbehavior and incident disclosure.
content_selection.evidence: Included: 'Cloudflare acquires Deno. The Deno team moves to Cloudflare Workers...' Excluded: 'Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims (TechCrunch)', 'SemiAnalysis: only 3.6% of 857 Chinese model releases had a safety result', 'Senate investigation: data center developers misled public on costs'.

selection_disagreements.story: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims
selection_disagreements.rationale: TechCrunch (Oct 8) reported an open letter from Wang, Korbak and Balesni to OpenAI's safety committees, and Yahoo, The Rundown, Android Headlines and others picked it up. It is squarely on the brief's safety and disclosure theme and adds OpenAI's internal side of the story. OpenAI cited a 'pattern of misconduct', while the researchers warned of a chilling effect and denied leaking to The Information.

selection_disagreements.story: SemiAnalysis: only 3.6% of 857 Chinese model releases had published safety results
selection_disagreements.rationale: This is an original SemiAnalysis report from Oct 8, covered by AI Weekly, FourWeekMBA, Inside AI and others. It found only 31 of 857 releases had a published safety result and just 9 had one at launch. It complements the brief's disclosure theme and its note that Chinese models dominate open-weight adoption.

selection_disagreements.story: Senate investigation: data center developers misled public on costs
selection_disagreements.rationale: This was a TIME exclusive (Oct 8), with follow-ups in Tom's Hardware and a Warren/Van Hollen/Blumenthal press release. The year-long probe of Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix covers NDAs, tax breaks and ratepayer costs. It is a significant AI-infrastructure policy story with no coverage at all in the brief.

selection_disagreements.story: Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro orders 15-20% citing AI-driven memory costs
selection_disagreements.rationale: Nikkei Asia broke this exclusive (Oct 9) and Reuters, Fortune and Yahoo Finance followed. It ties the AI data-center memory crunch to falling demand for flagship consumer hardware, and Apple shares fell about 1.9% premarket. It deserved at least a Briefly line.
This is a JavaScript-runtime and dev-infrastructure deal with no clear AI angle given in the brief. It took a Briefly slot that the more relevant excluded stories above should have had.
It is a minor embedding-model release with only a single-newsletter source. It is lower priority than the excluded safety and policy stories, which had wide coverage.

factual_accuracy.rationale: Nearly all the claims I checked match primary or high-quality sources. That covers the Anthropic report details (models, benchmarks, remediation, the October 8 notification note vs. TechCrunch's "Wednesday"), the OpenAI grader incident (seven identical 4s, the pristine-VM reasoning, three failed health checks), TechCrunch's figures on Arena, the math release and the usage policy, Memento 3's numbers on arXiv, the FT revenue and Nvidia–Reflection reports via Reuters and others, the TypeSafe and Manus rounds, Nadella's quotes, and Gemini's agent identities. I found a few small problems. Bloomberg Law's summary of the FT dates Reflection's $25B round to March, not April as the brief has it. OpenAI's alignment page doesn't mention extending monitoring to "all RL and evaluation traffic." Epoch's own summary gives 15% as the top result, so the brief's upper figure of ~35% traces only to explainx. I couldn't confirm the November 12 effective date for the usage policy. The brief flags its secondary and paywalled sourcing well throughout.
factual_accuracy.evidence: Brief: "Reflection's last round, in April, was at a $25B pre-money valuation" vs. Bloomberg Law's summary of the FT: Reflection "was last valued at $25b in a March funding round"; Epoch's own summary: models' "best efforts topped out at 15% of the performance gains from SDPO."

length_format.rationale: Headline count is 14, within the 8-15 target, and there are 10 deep-dives across the tiered sections (Policy 3, Research 2, Benchmarks 1, Industry 2, Products 2), which is at the upper edge of the 5-10 range; empty sections are correctly omitted. However, nearly every deep-dive far exceeds the 3-6 sentence target. The Anthropic item runs to roughly 20 sentences, and others such as the OpenAI grader, Decision models and Nvidia/Reflection items run 10-15. Several items also bundle two stories into one entry (Memento 3 + Arena, SI Force + Nadella). This is substantial over-length at the summary level, though the overall counts and structure comply.
length_format.evidence: The Anthropic deep-dive alone lists four behavior types, multiple named model cases, conflicting police-notification dates, benchmark names, a remediation list, and a Transluce quote, roughly 20 sentences against a 3-6 sentence target.

dedup.rationale: Every story that overlaps a prior edition carries an explicit label and adds new information. The math item adds outside scrutiny from the IAS advisory group and a Cambridge/KCL Lean-discrepancy paper. The Reflection item adds the reported Nvidia acquisition talks. The decision-model item adds Microsoft Decision-1, Liquid d1 and TypeSafe's $870M raise. The Anthropic incident report is a separate disclosure, honestly flagged as part of a broader thread. All other items (White House SI Force, OpenAI grader incident, OpenAI revenue revision, Epoch InnovationEval, Memento 3, Arena, Gemini Enterprise, Manus, Nadella, the usage policy) do not appear in the Oct 7–9 briefs, so there is no unlabelled or unjustified repetition.
dedup.evidence: "Follow-up: OpenAI's AI-generated math release from the October 7 and October 8 briefs; today adds outside scrutiny"; it also flags "Our October 8 brief cited 722 manuscripts; the discrepancy is unresolved."
